primary_decoupling.activity_to_decouple: Evaluate products by trying them before buying full-size
primary_decoupling.from_incumbent_bundle: Brick-and-mortar beauty retailers and major beauty brands (e.g., Sephora/department stores) that bundle evaluation with in-store testing as part of an end-to-end retail journey
primary_decoupling.customer_pain: Product evaluation is tightly tied to in-store testing, which requires a store visit and makes it harder for customers to evaluate products in their own at-home context over time (E7).
primary_decoupling.new_offering: A subscription-based, at-home trial service that delivers curated beauty samples monthly so customers can evaluate products at home before buying full-size (E2, E12).
primary_decoupling.why_customer_switches: They can adopt Birchbox just for the trial/evaluation step without changing where they buy full-size products—an archetypal decoupling move that “peel[s] away a portion of the customer’s value chain” while the disruptor and incumbent can still ‘share’ the customer (books/unlocking-the-customer-value-chain-chapter-1.md > Page 6) (E3).

do_not_decouple.reason: Jumping from the evaluation wedge into being the primary full-size purchase destination increases operational and channel conflict complexity and risks undermining the subscription-led at-home trial engine; it also drags Birchbox into the incumbent-controlled purchase stage (E8, E11) rather than strengthening the already-working discovery/evaluation decoupling (E2, E12).

do_not_decouple.activity: Repurchase favorites (and restart discovery/evaluation when needs change)
do_not_decouple.reason: Repurchase is historically part of the retailer/brand-controlled end-to-end journey (E10, E11) and would pressure Birchbox to build heavy commerce reliability across many SKUs; that over-extends beyond the current decoupled discovery/evaluation model anchored in monthly sample delivery (E2, E12).

do_not_decouple.activity: Use the product at home and assess satisfaction over time
do_not_decouple.reason: Owning long-term usage/satisfaction support would require deep product-performance guarantees and service obligations that are not core to the existing curated-sample disruption; Birchbox’s proven wedge is enabling at-home trial via samples, not managing the full at-home lifecycle (E2, E12).

do_not_decouple.activity: Recognize a need or desire to try a new beauty product (e.g., skincare, makeup, haircare)
do_not_decouple.reason: Need recognition is broad and diffuse; trying to ‘own’ it would dilute focus and reduce the sharpness of the decoupled wedge, whereas Birchbox already wins by intercepting customers specifically at discovery/evaluation through curated monthly samples (E12) rather than attempting to replace the entire incumbent-controlled journey (E11).
